title: Inference Demand Signal Map & Proxy Benchmarking Playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Sales and Support teams report increasing friction when certain customer workloads experience sudden latency/cost spikes due to model availability or degraded model variants. We lack a compact, repeatable way to surface 'demand signals' that predict when a customer or cohort will require a fallback model or reserved capacity, and we have no lightweight proxy benchmark to estimate how new open model variants behave on those demand patterns. Goal: produce a documented playbook and dashboard that maps production demand signals (query shape, token distribution, concurrency spikes, regional latency anomalies, error class spikes) to recommended operational actions (model variant fallback, autoscale bump, reserved capacity recommendations, customer outreach). Deliver a proxy benchmark harness and a small set of canonical query skeletons (3-5 per vertical) to rapidly evaluate candidate models for admission into fallback pools. Outcome: reduce unexpected customer impact hours from model supply issues by 30% and cut manual triage time by 40% within 3 months of rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy defined with at least 8 signals and authoritative telemetry sources for each
Proxy benchmark harness built and runnable by infra/eng with sample results for 6 candidate models
Dashboard prototype (Console) showing per-customer/cohort signal score and recommended action
Runbook with action mappings and SLA-driven thresholds published to Confluence
Pilot completed with two mid-market customers showing measurable reduction in incident triage time

notes: Proxy benchmark approach: use canonical query skeletons with variable payload lengths and token distributions; measure p95 latency, median cost/token, token generation throughput, and failure modes (timeouts, OOM).
Edge-case: embeddings-heavy customers may not be well-served by text-generation signals; plan to add an embeddings-signal pass in iteration 2.

Operational trade-offs: aggressive alert thresholds reduce missed incidents but increase false positives and manual actions; propose confidence-scored actions to let SRE/CS choose autopilot or manual mode.
Longer-term: integrate with model-scouting signals so new entrants can be evaluated against the proxy bench automatically when added to model catalog.
